MA4102 overview

MA4102 Topic Guide

Entanglement and Reduced States

Trace out one subsystem, then interpret the remaining density matrix.

Purpose

Past papers repeatedly ask whether a bipartite state is entangled and to quantify it through a reduced state.Exam use: Subsystem order, density operator, partial-trace matches, reduced eigenvalues/purity and criterion are explicit.

Question plan

  1. Write |ψ⟩ in a product basis |a⟩|b⟩.
  2. Form ρAB=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|.
  3. Take ρA=TrB(ρAB).
  4. Use purity or S(ρA) to conclude for a pure bipartite state.
  5. Question interpretation: For decide entanglement of a pure bipartite state, attempt factorisation or compute a reduced-state rank/purity; for mixed states do not reuse the pure-state test blindly.

Notation and derivation

TrB(|a⟩⟨c|⊗|b⟩⟨d|)=⟨d|b⟩|a⟩⟨c|. A pure product state has pure reduction; a pure entangled state has mixed reductions.Rapid recall: A pure bipartite state is separable iff its coefficient matrix has rank 1 iff either reduced density matrix is pure; partial trace satisfies Tr_B(|i><j| tensor |k><l|)=delta_kl |i><j|.Exam workflow: Form |psi><psi|, trace matching basis indices of the discarded subsystem, then compute determinant, rank or purity of the reduction.

Worked calculation

For |Φ+⟩=(|00⟩+|11⟩)/√2, cross terms vanish under TrB, so ρA=½(|0⟩⟨0|+|1⟩⟨1|)=I/2. Its purity is 1/2, hence |Φ+⟩ is entangled.

Practice 1 — certify a two-qubit state as maximally entangled [9 marks]

Prompt. For the supplied four-amplitude state, form its coefficient matrix, reduce to subsystem A, and decide whether it is maximally entangled. Question-demand diagnosis. The conclusion must be justified by a reduction or rank criterion for a pure bipartite state. Fastest route. Use ρA=CC†, then inspect its eigenvalues or purity. Topic-specific trap. Four nonzero product-basis amplitudes do not by themselves prove entanglement.

For |psi>=(|00>+|01>+|10>-|11>)/2, coefficient matrix C=(1/2)[[1,1],[1,-1]]. Then rho_A=CC^dagger=I/2, with purity 1/2 and rank 2. Therefore |psi> is maximally entangled. Although four product-basis amplitudes appear, no product factorisation exists because det C=-1/2 !=0.

Graduated exam bridge

1. Reduce |00⟩ and decide whether it is entangled. Check: ρA=|0⟩⟨0|, purity 1.

2. For a|00⟩+b|11⟩, find S(ρA). Check: eigenvalues are |a|2,|b|2.

Practice 2 — partially entangled Bell-type state [8 marks]

Prompt. Find the entanglement entropy of √3/2|00>+1/2|11>. Question-demand diagnosis. Entropy is obtained from the reduced state’s eigenvalues, not from the four-state vector entries directly. Fastest route. Trace out either qubit and evaluate the binary entropy of 3/4,1/4. Topic-specific trap. A state can be entangled without being maximally entangled.

Paper-style synthesis: for |phi>=sqrt(3)/2|00>+1/2|11>, find entanglement entropy. Check reduced eigenvalues are 3/4,1/4, so S=-3/4 log2(3/4)-1/4 log2(1/4), strictly between 0 and 1.

Mistakes

  • Tracing out labels rather than matching them.
  • Using mixedness of the whole pure state.
  • Declaring a state separable from one measurement outcome.
  • Recovery rule: Classical correlation in a mixed state is not automatically entanglement; state which criterion applies to the class of states given.

Checklist

  • I can partial-trace a two-qubit state.
  • I connect reduced purity to entanglement.
  • I use the pure-state condition when making that inference.
  • Final 60-second audit: Subsystem order, density operator, partial-trace matches, reduced eigenvalues/purity and criterion are explicit.
